subject: math
title: Numbers to 100 000: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 5 Numbers to 100 000 Math Worksheets: Place Value, Comparing and Rounding (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 100 000, using appropriate tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on numbers to 100 000 for the Ontario curriculum: place value, the value of each digit, expanded form, comparing and ordering, number lines and rounding with real-life numbers. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 4 in 45 300 is worth 40 000.
key_sub: Write three digits after the space: forty thousand five hundred three is 40 503, not 4503. To compare, count the digits first, then compare from the left.
body_html:
Place value to 100 000

Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. Ten ten thousands make 100 000 (one hundred thousand). Big numbers are split into groups of three digits. In Canada we leave a small space between the groups (45 300), not a comma. A 4-digit number has no space (4503).

Place value disks show the same thing. Find the value of each group, then add.

Words to digits

Write forty thousand five hundred three in digits.

Forty thousand → 40. Five hundred three → 503 (always three digits after the space).

Answer: 40 503 (not 4503)

The value of a digit

The digit is the symbol. Its value depends on its place. In 47 125 the digit 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7000.

Expanded form and decomposing

Expanded form shows the value of each digit: 68 725 = 60 000 + 8000 + 700 + 20 + 5. Leave out the zeros: 40 503 = 40 000 + 500 + 3.

Decompose

Write 45 300 in three ways.

Expanded form: 40 000 + 5000 + 300. It is also 45 thousands and 3 hundreds, or 453 hundreds.

Answer: 40 000 + 5000 + 300 = 45 thousands + 3 hundreds = 453 hundreds

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 5-digit number is greater than any 4-digit number. If both have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

63 405 ☐ 63 450

Ten thousands: 6 = 6. Thousands: 3 = 3. Hundreds: 4 = 4. Tens: 0 < 5.

Answer: 63 405 < 63 450

Number lines and rounding

On a number line, work out the size of each space first. To round, look at the digit one place to the right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down.

Round 67 850 to the nearest …Look atAnswer
ten thousandthe thousands digit: 770 000
thousandthe hundreds digit: 868 000
hundredthe tens digit: 567 900

Big numbers in everyday life

We see numbers to 100 000 in crowds at hockey and football games, in the populations of towns and cities, and in money raised for events like the Terry Fox Run. News reports often round them: 34 862 fans becomes “about 35 000 fans”.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out a zero (forty thousand five hundred three → 4503)Write three digits after the space: 40 | 503 → 40 503
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 47 125 is 7)It is in the thousands place: 7000
Counting the disks (4 + 5 + 3 = 12)Add the values: 40 000 + 5000 + 300 = 45 300
Comparing the first digits only (9876 > 10 234)Count the digits first: 10 234 > 9876
Thinking every space on a number line is 1000Work out the space first: 45 000 to 46 000 in 10 spaces is 100 each
Rounding twice (34 512 → 35 000 → 40 000)Round the number you started with: 30 000

faq.q: What number skills are in the Grade 5 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 5 students read, represent, compose and decompose whole numbers up to 100 000 (B1.1) and compare and order them (B1.2). They also describe how big numbers are used in everyday life, such as crowds, populations and money.

faq.q: Why do Canadian students write 45 300 with a space instead of a comma?
faq.a: Canada follows the SI style: numbers with 5 or more digits are split into groups of three with a small space, and 4-digit numbers have no space (4503). This avoids mix-ups with the decimal comma used in French.

faq.q: How do you write forty thousand five hundred three in numbers?
faq.a: Write 40 for the thousands part and 503 for the rest: 40 503. The part after the space always has three digits, so the number is not 4503.

faq.q: How do you round a 5-digit number to the nearest thousand?
faq.a: Look at the hundreds digit. If it is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, keep the thousands digit and change the rest to 0. So 67 850 rounds to 68 000 and 45 300 rounds to 45 000.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 4 × 10 000 = 40 000; 5 × 1000 = 5000; 3 × 100 = 300. Add them: 45 300. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 3 × 10 000 = 30 000; 2 × 100 = 200; 1 × 10 = 10; 6 × 1 = 6. Add them: 30 216. There are no thousands, so write 0 in that place. Do not just count the disks: each disk has its own value.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 63 527 the red 6 is in the ten thousands place.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 28 914 the red 8 is in the thousands place.

items.q: In 74 381, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: In 74 381: ten thousands 7, thousands 4, hundreds 3, tens 8, ones 1. The thousands digit is 4.

items.q: Which number is forty thousand five hundred three?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: forty thousand → 40. Then write the rest with three digits: five hundred three → 503. So the number is 40 503.

items.q: Which number is seventy-two thousand eighty?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: seventy-two thousand → 72. Then write the rest with three digits: eighty → 080. So the number is 72 080.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 1 × 10 000 = 10 000; 2 × 1000 = 2000; 4 × 10 = 40. Add them: 12 040. There are no hundreds or ones, so write 0 in those places.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands. In 50 762 the red 7 is in the hundreds place.

items.q: How do you write 60 405 in words?
items.e: Split 60 405 into the thousands part and the rest: 60 thousand and 405. Say each part: sixty thousand four hundred five.

items.q: Which number is thirty thousand six?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: thirty thousand → 30. Then write the rest with three digits: six → 006. So the number is 30 006.

items.q: In 59 026, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: In 59 026: ten thousands 5, thousands 9, hundreds 0, tens 2, ones 6. The hundreds digit is 0. The 0 shows there are no hundreds.

items.q: How many thousands make 10 000?
items.e: Count by thousands: 1000, 2000, 3000 … 10 000. That is 10 thousands. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What number do the place value disks show?
items.e: Find the value of each group: 2 × 10 000 = 20 000; 5 × 10 = 50; 1 × 1 = 1. Add them: 20 051. There are no thousands or hundreds, so write 0 in those places.

items.q: Which number is fifteen thousand four hundred?
items.e: Say the thousands part first: fifteen thousand → 15. Then write the rest with three digits: four hundred → 400. So the number is 15 400. Fifteen is 15, not 50.

items.q: How do you write 18 070 in words?
items.e: Split 18 070 into the thousands part and the rest: 18 thousand and 70. Say each part: eighteen thousand seventy. Eighteen is 18, eighty is 80.

items.q: Ten groups of 10 000 make what number?
items.e: 10 × 10 000 = 100 000. Count by ten thousands: 10 000, 20 000 … 100 000. Ten ten thousands make one hundred thousand.

items.q: Which number is one hundred thousand?
items.e: One hundred thousand is 100 groups of 1000. Write 100 for the thousands part and 000 for the rest: 100 000. It has 6 digits. (10 000 is ten thousand.)

items.q: How do you write 47 012 in words?
items.e: Split 47 012 into the thousands part and the rest: 47 thousand and 12. Say each part: forty-seven thousand twelve.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 99 999?
items.e: 99 999 + 1: every 9 becomes 0 as you regroup, and a 1 goes in the hundred thousands place: 100 000. (99 998 is 1 less.)

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 2 thousands = 2000. The digit is 2, but its value is 2000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 3 ten thousands = 30 000. The digit is 3, but its value is 30 000.

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 47 125?
items.e: The 7 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 7 thousands = 7000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7000.

items.q: What is the value of the 3 in 23 609?
items.e: The 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3 thousands = 3000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3000.

items.q: The town of Lakeview has 28 460 people. What is the value of the 8?
items.e: 28 460 is 2 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 4 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones. The 8 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 8000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 9 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 9 hundreds = 900. The digit is 9, but its value is 900.

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 70 284?
items.e: The 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70 000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70 000.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the ten thousands place?
items.e: 63 205 has 6 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones. The ten thousands digit is 6.

items.q: Which number has 0 thousands?
items.e: 40 516 is 4 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 5 hundreds, 1 ten and 6 ones. The other numbers all have 4 or 5 thousands.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

items.q: What is the value of the 5 in 91 538?
items.e: The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the thousands place?
items.e: 74 019 has 7 ten thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 1 ten, 9 ones. The thousands digit is 4.

items.q: 37 800 = ☐ thousands and 8 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 37 800 = 37 000 + 800. 37 000 is 37 thousands. So 37 800 = 37 thousands and 8 hundreds. (7 is only the thousands digit.)

items.q: In 90 407, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 90 407 is 9 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. The tens digit is 0: there are no tens.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 9 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 9 thousands = 9000. The digit is 9, but its value is 9000.

items.q: What is the value of the 2 in 46 820?
items.e: The 2 is in the tens place, so it is worth 2 tens = 20. The digit is 2, but its value is 20.

items.q: Which number has a 0 in the hundreds place?
items.e: 58 037 has 5 ten thousands, 8 thousands, 0 hundreds, 3 tens, 7 ones. The hundreds digit is 0.

items.q: 26 000 = ☐ hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 1000 = 10 hundreds, so 26 thousands = 26 × 10 = 260 hundreds. Check: 260 × 100 = 26 000.

items.q: The 4 in 40 000 is worth how many times the 4 in 4000?
items.e: The first 4 is worth 40 000. The second 4 is worth 4000. 40 000 ÷ 4000 = 10. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. (36 000 is the difference, not how many times.)

items.q: In 55 500, the first 5 is worth how many times the second 5?
items.e: The first 5 is in the ten thousands place: 50 000. The second 5 is in the thousands place: 5000. 50 000 ÷ 5000 = 10.

items.q: What is 68 725 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: ten thousands 6 = 60 000, thousands 8 = 8000, hundreds 7 = 700, tens 2 = 20, ones 5 = 5. That is 60 000 + 8000 + 700 + 20 + 5.

items.q: What is 45 300 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: ten thousands 4 = 40 000, thousands 5 = 5000, hundreds 3 = 300. That is 40 000 + 5000 + 300. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.

items.q: What number is 80 000 + 600 + 4?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 80 000 + 600 + 4 → 80 604.

items.q: What number is 30 000 + 7000 + 20?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 30 000 + 7000 + 20 → 37 020.

items.q: 60 000 + ☐ + 700 + 20 + 5 = 68 725. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 68 725 has 8 in the thousands place. That is worth 8000.

items.q: ☐ + 3000 + 40 + 2 = 53 042. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 53 042 has 5 in the ten thousands place. That is worth 50 000.

items.q: What is 40 503 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: ten thousands 4 = 40 000, hundreds 5 = 500, ones 3 = 3. That is 40 000 + 500 + 3. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.

items.q: What number is 50 000 + 9?
items.e: Put each value in its place and write 0 in every empty place. 50 000 + 9 → 50 009.

items.q: 70 000 + 400 + ☐ = 70 409. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 70 409 has 9 in the ones place. That is worth 9.

items.q: What is 72 080 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: ten thousands 7 = 70 000, thousands 2 = 2000, tens 8 = 80. That is 70 000 + 2000 + 80. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.
The parts are not in order. Sort them from the greatest place: 20 000 + 4000 + 300 + 60 + 1 = 24 361. Do not write the digits in the order you see them.

items.q: 10 000 + 5000 + ☐ + 6 = 15 086. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 15 086 has 8 in the tens place. That is worth 80.

items.q: What is 93 016 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: ten thousands 9 = 90 000, thousands 3 = 3000, tens 1 = 10, ones 6 = 6. That is 90 000 + 3000 + 10 + 6. A 0 adds nothing, so it is left out.
Work out each part: 9 × 10 000 = 90 000, 6 × 100 = 600, 5 × 1 = 5. Add them: 90 605. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: 45 300 = ☐ hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 45 300 = 45 thousands and 3 hundreds. 45 thousands = 450 hundreds. 450 + 3 = 453 hundreds. Check: 453 × 100 = 45 300.
Work out each part: 7 × 10 000 = 70 000, 2 × 10 = 20, 9 × 1 = 9. Add them: 70 029. Write 0 in every empty place.

items.q: What number is 3 ten thousands, 14 thousands and 2 hundreds?
items.e: 3 ten thousands = 30 000 and 14 thousands = 14 000. 30 000 + 14 000 + 200 = 44 200. Do not write 14 inside the number: 14 thousands is 1 ten thousand and 4 thousands.

items.q: 26 400 = 1 ten thousand, ☐ thousands and 4 hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 26 400 = 2 ten thousands, 6 thousands and 4 hundreds. Trade 1 ten thousand for 10 thousands: 10 + 6 = 16 thousands. Check: 10 000 + 16 000 + 400 = 26 400.

items.q: Which is another way to make 52 700?
items.e: 4 ten thousands = 40 000 and 12 thousands = 12 000. 40 000 + 12 000 + 700 = 52 700. (The others make 42 700, 62 700 and 59 000.)

items.q: Which is not equal to 32 000?
items.e: 3 ten thousands and 2 hundreds = 30 000 + 200 = 30 200, not 32 000. 32 thousands = 32 000, 320 hundreds = 32 000 and 20 000 + 12 000 = 32 000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 3 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 45 300 > 45 030.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 10 234 has 5 digits and 9876 has only 4, so 10 234 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 5 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds. So 36 512 > 36 215. 36 512 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 8999 has only 4 digits, so it is the least, even though it starts with 8. Every 5-digit number is at least 10 000.

items.q: Put 45 300, 43 500, 45 030 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 ten thousands. Thousands: 3 < 5, so 43 500 is the least. 45 300 and 45 030 both have 5 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 3, so 45 030 < 45 300. Order: 43 500, 45 030, 45 300.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 0 tens. So 63 450 > 63 405.

items.q: Which number is between 45 000 and 46 000?
items.e: A number between 45 000 and 46 000 has 4 ten thousands and 5 thousands. 45 870 fits. 46 500 is too big, 44 990 is too small and 4580 has only 4 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 7, 2, 9, 4 and 1 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the ten thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 7, 4, 2, 1. The greatest number is 97 421.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 7989 has only 4 digits, so it is the least. For the 5-digit numbers, compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 0 tens. So 70 890 > 70 809. 70 890 is the greatest.

items.q: Put 61 204, 16 402, 62 104 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: Ten thousands: 1 < 6, so 16 402 is the least. 61 204 and 62 104 both have 6 ten thousands. Thousands: 2 > 1, so 62 104 > 61 204. Order: 62 104, 61 204, 16 402.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the ten thousands: 8 ten thousands is more than 7 ten thousands. So 80 091 > 79 999.

items.q: Which number is between 79 900 and 80 100?
items.e: 80 015 is more than 80 000 and less than 80 100, so it is between 79 900 and 80 100. 80 150 is too big, 79 090 is too small and 8010 has only 4 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 5, 0, 8, 3 and 6 once. What is the least 5-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 5-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 3. Then 0, 5, 6, 8: 30 568. (03 568 is just 3568, which has only 4 digits.)

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 6 tens is more than 0 tens. So 42 560 > 42 506. 42 506 is the least.

items.q: Put 9950, 10 500, 10 050, 9505 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: The 4-digit numbers are less than the 5-digit numbers. 9505 < 9950 (hundreds: 5 < 9). 10 050 < 10 500 (hundreds: 0 < 5). Order: 9505, 9950, 10 050, 10 500.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 8 tens is more than 2 tens. So 51 782 > 51 728.

items.q: 4☐ 215 > 47 300. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The ten thousands are the same. Compare the thousands: the box must be 7 or more. If it is 7, compare the hundreds: 2 < 3, so 47 215 is too small. 48 215 > 47 300.

items.q: Use each of the digits 6, 0, 2, 0 and 9 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Biggest digit first: 9, then 6, then 2. The two 0s go last, in the tens and ones places: 96 200.

items.q: Put 99 000, 100 000, 90 999, 99 900 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 100 000 has 6 digits, so it is the greatest. Then compare the 5-digit numbers: 99 900 > 99 000 (hundreds: 9 > 0) and 99 000 > 90 999 (thousands: 9 > 0). Order: 100 000, 99 900, 99 000, 90 999.

items.q: 62 ☐80 < 62 450. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The ten thousands and thousands are the same. Compare the hundreds: the box must be 4 or less. If it is 4, compare the tens: 8 > 5, so 62 480 is too big. 62 380 < 62 450.

sets.title: Number lines, rounding and real-life numbers

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 50 000: 60 000, 70 000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 40 000 to 50 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1000, not 100. The arrow is 3 spaces after 40 000: 43 000.

items.q: Round 45 300 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Nearest thousand: 45 300 is between 45 000 and 46 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down. So 45 300 rounds to 45 000.

items.q: Round 67 850 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Nearest thousand: 67 850 is between 67 000 and 68 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up. So 67 850 rounds to 68 000. Do not just drop the hundreds: 67 000 is cutting off, not rounding.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 45 000 to 46 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100, not 1000. The arrow is 3 spaces after 45 000: 45 300.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 20 000 to 30 000 there are only 5 equal spaces, so each space is 10 000 ÷ 5 = 2000. The arrow is 3 spaces after 20 000: 22 000, 24 000, 26 000. (23 000 counts each space as 1000.)

items.q: Round 34 512 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Nearest ten thousand: 34 512 is between 30 000 and 40 000. Look at the thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. So 34 512 rounds to 30 000. Round the number you started with. Do not round to 35 000 first.

items.q: Round 85 096 to the nearest ten thousand.
items.e: Nearest ten thousand: 85 096 is between 80 000 and 90 000. Look at the thousands digit: 5. 5 or more, so round up. So 85 096 rounds to 90 000.

items.q: Round 29 961 to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Nearest hundred: 29 961 is between 29 900 and 30 000. Look at the tens digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. So 29 961 rounds to 30 000. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand, so 29 900 becomes 30 000.

items.q: There were 34 862 fans at a football game. A news report rounds the crowd to the nearest thousand. What number does it report?
items.e: Nearest thousand: 34 862 is between 34 000 and 35 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up. So 34 862 rounds to 35 000.

items.q: Maple Creek has 18 406 people. Pine Bay has 18 460 people. Which town has more people?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 6 tens is more than 0 tens. So 18 460 > 18 406. Pine Bay has more people.

items.q: Three towns have 27 095, 29 750 and 27 509 people. Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: Thousands: 7 < 9, so 29 750 is the greatest. 27 095 and 27 509 both have 7 thousands. Hundreds: 0 < 5, so 27 095 < 27 509. Order: 27 095, 27 509, 29 750.

items.q: Schools in one city raised forty-five thousand three hundred dollars for the Terry Fox Run. Write the amount in numbers.
items.e: Say the thousands part first: forty-five thousand → 45. Then write the rest with three digits: three hundred → 300. So the number is 45 300. The amount is $45 300.

items.q: Noah’s mystery number has 7 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones. What is it?
items.e: Write one digit for each place, with 0 for the empty places: 7, 0, 4, 0, 2. That is 70 402.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the number of people at a sold-out NHL hockey game?
items.e: NHL arenas hold about 15 000 to 21 000 people, so about 19 000 is a good estimate. About 190 or 1900 is far too few, and 190 000 is more people than live in many Canadian cities.

items.q: A city’s population, rounded to the nearest ten thousand, is 60 000. Which could be the real population?
items.e: Numbers from 55 000 up to 64 999 round to 60 000. 56 780 has 6 thousands, so it rounds up to 60 000. 54 990 rounds to 50 000, 65 000 rounds up to 70 000, and 6500 is far too small.

items.q: A sugar bush has 15 000 maple trees. The workers tap them in groups of 1000. How many groups is that?
items.e: 15 000 = 15 thousands. So there are 15 groups of 1000. Check: 15 × 1000 = 15 000.

items.q: Volunteers counted 24 680 Canada geese at a wetland. Round the count to the nearest hundred.
items.e: Nearest hundred: 24 680 is between 24 600 and 24 700. Look at the tens digit: 8. 5 or more, so round up. So 24 680 rounds to 24 700.

items.q: A city had 89 650 people. Ten years later it has 10 000 more people. How many people live there now?
items.e: Adding 10 000 changes the ten thousands digit: 8 ten thousands + 1 = 9 ten thousands. 89 650 + 10 000 = 99 650. (90 650 adds only 1000.)

items.q: Sofia’s town has planted 25 000 trees. It plants 10 000 more each year. How many trees will it have planted after 3 more years?
items.e: Count on by 10 000s: 35 000, 45 000, 55 000. After 3 more years the town will have planted 55 000 trees. (28 000 adds only 3000.)
